approach: Root cause, from the code and history. `checks::failure_section` (checks.rs:373-419) is the one place a failed check's output is chosen for storage. It knows only two things: a runner marker (`failures:`, `panicked at`, `---- x stdout ----`, `test result: FAILED`) and a cleanup HEADER line (`Post job cleanup`, `Post Run `, `Cleaning up orphan processes`, checks.rs:345-351). Header-first cutting landed in fe42b01 (HISTORY.txt:733, 2026-11-07; CHANGELOG.md:1164-1166). By job id date, five of the six sightings (20261027-054225-ycks, 20261029-204942-2zqw, 20261030-033234-vm1m, 20261106-022423-vdtn, 20261106-045349-f6x6) predate it. The one sighting after it (introspection 20261114-022748-gmm5, job 20261114-013056-pkhp) says the failing unit's output was lost behind the shard summary. A job can run later than its id date and `records/` is absent from the snapshot, so which log shape each job had cannot be shown; the plan covers both shapes. Two gaps remain in the code: (1) A marker-less failing unit (compile error, crash). `xtask test-shard` runs every unit even after one fails (xtask/src/shard.rs:315-327), prints `== shard k/n: <unit>` before each (shard.rs:317, xtask/src/main.rs:112-114) and ends with `error: shard k of n: X of Y units failed: <units>` (shard.rs:332-337, main.rs:64). With no runner marker, `failure_section` keeps a plain tail of the last 200 lines (checks.rs:402-403), which is the later passing units' output plus that summary. The log itself names the failing unit, but nothing reads it. (2) A cleanup block with no recognised header (cancelled or cut-off log, header form not matched, or git credential-removal lines above the last header line) falls through to a plain tail of cleanup text, and nothing tells the reader that no failing section exists. Fix: (A) In gh/client.rs, next to `failing_units` (client.rs:264, which already splits at `== shard `), a new `failed_units_only(log)` reads the final `units failed:` summary. For a log with no runner marker it keeps each named unit's own part, collapses the passing units to one `(output of N passing units not kept: ...)` line, and keeps the summary and what follows. `detail_from_job_logs` passes that reduced log to `failure_section`. (B) In checks.rs, recognition of cleanup by content, with a bounded backward walk from the end, stays the one cleanup recogniser. A log with no failing section gets ONE trailing note, counted inside the 200-line and 64 KiB limits. (C) `CheckFailure::of` passes the stored output through `failure_section`. No record shape, admission or gate code changes, and no refusal rule is added. Only the five listed deliverable files change: the earlier plan's edits to gh/tests.rs and ci_result.rs are dropped.

decisions.choice: Read the failing unit from the log's own summary and keep its output: `failed_units_only(log: &str) -> Option<String>` in gh/client.rs. It runs only when the log has no runner marker (`checks::has_failing_section` false). It takes the LAST line that, after an optional `error: ` prefix, starts `shard ` and holds ` units failed: `, and splits the units on `; `. It splits the log at `== shard k/n: <unit>` lines (the same literal `failing_units` uses at client.rs:267). For each unit named in the summary it keeps the header line and the part up to the next header or the summary line. Each run of unnamed (passing) units becomes one line `(output of N passing units not kept: a; b)`. The summary line and everything after it are kept (the summary, `##[error]`, cleanup), and everything before the first header is dropped. It returns None (old path) with no summary, no header for a named unit, or any runner marker. `detail_from_job_logs` calls `failure_section` on the reduced log, and a reduced log counts as having a failing section for the note.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. The information the failing stage lacked is which unit failed, and the log holds it. Reduced output is compact, so the 3000-byte send-back tail (send_back.rs:297) and the verifier brief's last 60 lines (briefs.rs:1110-1127) still hold the unit's error lines, and `with_failure_detail`'s second pass (checks.rs:443-445) leaves it unchanged (at most 200 lines, no cleanup). Doing it in client.rs next to `failing_units` and before `failure_section` keeps `failure_section` a string cutter used by local runs, and adds no cleanup recogniser outside checks.rs. The no-marker precondition leaves every existing marker log (gh/tests.rs 494, 537, 607, 674, 726, 746; run/tests.rs:7724) on the old path. Limit: a failing unit part longer than the shard's window loses its first lines, and a log that mixes a marker unit with a marker-less failing unit keeps the old behavior.

decisions.choice: One cleanup recogniser, in checks.rs. Split `is_cleanup_header` (the three existing forms, `##[group]` prefix ignored) out of `is_cleanup_line`; `is_cleanup_line` becomes header or content: `[command]/usr/bin/git `, `Temporarily overriding HOME`, `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Removing includeIf`, `Complete job`, `Evaluate and set job outputs`, `##[warning]Node.js`. The bare `/usr/bin/git ` form is dropped. Rewrite the doc comment to 'any line of CI runner cleanup text, not only the one that starts the block'. `failure_section` first cuts at the first header at or after the anchor's next line (`floor`: anchor + 1, else 0), else the end. `cleanup_start(lines, floor)` then walks back from that point over blank lines, recognised lines and at most `CLEANUP_GAP = 1` consecutive unrecognised lines. It stops at a `##[group]Run ` step start, at `floor`, or at the second unrecognised line, and returns the earliest recognised line it reached. The block is cut from there.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 5 and the round-2 findings 2 and 6. Only `[command]/usr/bin/git ` is cited from the actions toolkit; no log cited here has a bare `/usr/bin/git ` line, and the function also runs on local output (checks.rs:618). A walk from the END can strip only a trailing block, so checkout git lines at the start of a job log are not chosen. The `##[group]Run ` boundary separates the checkout block from the failing step. The gap of 1 covers `git version 2.x` and extraheader key lines between git commands. Idempotence: after a pass the last kept non-blank lines are two unrecognised lines, a step start or `floor`, so a second pass (with_failure_detail on the stored tail, CheckFailure::of) cuts nothing, with the trailing note counted as one of those unrecognised lines. Input forms and their tests (log lines, not readings): header then block (existing checks.rs:857); no header, block at the end (new test a); block without the orphan line and with interleaved plain lines (b); `##[error]` then block, no header (c); checkout lines at the log's start kept (d); header last with git lines above it (e); only cleanup (f); empty or blank input (g); a ci.yml-shaped log with the header present (h); a cleanup-looking line before the section (existing checks.rs:879). `refusal_corpus.rs` (lines 1-15) runs request and reading shapes through the reading gate; none of these forms is a reading or request, so no corpus case maps to them and none is added. The criterion 7 guard command is still run.

In `detail_from_job_logs`, a readable shard has a section when its log has a marker or `failed_units_only` returned Some. A shard is named in the note when it has none AND (its conclusion is not `failure` OR its stored section is not the whole log: `section.trim_end() != log.trim_end()`). Before computing `per_lines` and `per_bytes`, the code reserves 1 line and the byte length of a note naming every shard without a section (plus the existing 1 line for a `failing units:` line); that is an upper bound on the final note.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 6 (the wording no longer says 'the lines above' for every shard) and keeps the round-2 answer that the last line survives every tail reader: `failure_section`'s branches keep the end (checks.rs:394-406, 417-418), `CheckFailure::of` keeps the last 3000 bytes (send_back.rs:297), the verifier brief keeps the last 60 lines (briefs.rs:1110-1127) after `check_result_view` strips only a leading units line (verify.rs:75-86). The second clause leaves gh/tests.rs:578-590 as is: its log is two lines, concluded `failure`, has no cleanup, and is stored whole, so it gets no note and `ends_with("build broke\n")` still holds. That avoids editing a file outside the deliverables (finding 1). A cancelled or timed-out shard with no section always gets the note, which is criterion 2. The reserve keeps one shard at 199 lines plus the note, and three shards at 3 x (65 + 1 header) + 1 = 199, so the 200-line re-cut in with_failure_detail drops nothing.

risks.risk: Cleanup recognition is a list of known strings. A new runner cleanup form, or two or more consecutive unrecognised lines inside a headerless block, leaves some cleanup text in the record.

The content list covers the git, Node and Complete-job forms in the brief's log shape, and the gap of 1 covers interleaved plain lines. The trailing note still says when a shard had no failing test section. The CHANGELOG says recognition is by known text and claims no zero residual noise.

risks.risk: A cut removes real output: a local check whose output ends in cleanup-looking lines, or whose first line is a cleanup header (read as cleanup-only and replaced by the note).
risks.mitigation: The cut never goes before the last runner marker or `##[error]` line, stops at a `##[group]Run ` step start and after two consecutive unrecognised lines, and generic forms such as `git version ` and `##[group]` are not matched alone. `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE` is returned only when non-blank input was fully removed. The existing tests at checks.rs:857-930 and the new checkout-lines test must pass.

risks.risk: The six jobs' logs are not available (`records/` is absent from the snapshot), so which log shape each had is not shown, and five of six sightings predate fe42b01 by job id date, so the reduction (post-fix evidence from one sighting) and the content recognition (older shape) each address one shape without proof.

demonstrations.observes: One added entry. It names the failure class `failed-check-output-is-ci-noise-cause-of-test-failure-invisible` and the jobs 20261106-022423-vdtn, 20261106-045349-f6x6 and 20261027-054225-ycks. It states the root cause as what the code did, and dates the earlier header fix (fe42b01, 2026-11-07). The cause: `failure_section` knew only runner markers and a cleanup header; the `== shard` lines and the `units failed:` summary that name the failing unit were not read, so a marker-less failing unit gave way to the last 200 lines of later passing units; a block with no recognised header, or with git credential-removal lines above the header, fell through to a plain tail of cleanup text; and nothing said that no failing section was found. It says what the record stores now: the failing unit's own output with the passing units collapsed to one line, or the failing section, or the last pre-cleanup lines with one trailing note naming the shards with no failing test section; `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE` only when a non-empty log held only cleanup; empty output unchanged. It says recognition is by known text, so unknown cleanup forms can still appear, and that a mixed marker and marker-less failing log keeps the old behavior. It states that the logs of the six jobs were not available, so no claim is made about their shape. It states no refusal rule is added (0% of readings newly refused) and that the drain test and a base-tree rerun are not part of the change. It lists the tests with their commands and states only what the diff does.
